correctness.rationale: The uniquely determined distance vector with minimum j at b is a↦max(j,d(a,b)). Its nearest set is exactly the closed radius-j ball at b. The finite extension property realizes each such vector arbitrarily many times (add new points mutually at distance 1); homogeneity determines the complete type by the vector. Thus the polynomial is exactly the three unordered radius-wise size marginals. For n>=t, m>=1 and the subset-of-parts encoding filled by ones gives p(t)>=2^k>=n². The size-t radius-two balls preserve the chosen unordered set of m distinct refinements in the isometry type; the optional residual ball is distinguishable since r<t. Radius two and radius three are fixed, leaving at most p(n) polynomial values among binom(p(t),m) distinct hierarchies. The binomial lower bound follows by bounding each product factor (P-i)/(m-i)>=P/m; the partition upper bound follows from the Euler product and e^x-1>=x. Finally m log n is of order n/log n and dominates the O(sqrt(n)) subtraction. No upper bound or claim of a new small collision is part of the Finding.

Independent Euler-product coefficients at t=860 give p(t)=77169232591877674590168543277 and the stated lower-bound exponent at n=10^6 is about 13488.52. originality.rationale: The two-marginal fiber problem is meaningful and the proof is correct, but its claimed quantitative advance is already a routine fixed-outer-partition specialization of Cayley's known colored/double-partition enumeration. In that exact prior model a part of size s has p(s) possible colors (the internal size partition). Fix the outer partition to m parts of size t and one part of size r if r>0, and, for the residual part, fix one color. The cited multiset-of-colored-parts description gives binom(p(t)+m-1,m) possible types, including the narrower binom(p(t),m) distinct-color subfamily. The remaining marginal has at most p(n) values by definition. Hence the exact finite lower bound in the Finding, even its version with distinct refinements, follows mechanically from the known enumeration, the standard ball/type dictionary and one pigeonhole. The displayed exponential estimate just uses standard partition bounds for this coefficient. This is demonstrable mathematical implication, not a claim that Cayley's text explicitly discusses model-theoretic types, or a rejection based on unavailable sources.
residual_risks: The exact historical occurrence of the displayed graded-type wording is undetermined, as is any more precise published fiber asymptotic. The conclusion is coverage by direct implication, not verbatim prior publication. Kaneiwa's full text was unavailable in the inspected routes.

value.rationale: Quantifying nesting ambiguity is motivated, but the presented lower bound extracts one elementary colored-partition coefficient and divides by the total number of possible marginals. It does not identify particular large fibers or reveal geometry, optimal scales or a matching upper bound. The parameter choice and exclusion of repeated colors offer a weaker version of the immediate with-repetition count without a separate scientific reason to prefer that restriction. There is no independently valuable remainder that can be saved by rephrasing the same bound.
